I've completed all safe local execution. Here's my analysis and structured summary.

## Execution Report

I exercised the `cloudrouter` CLI skill safely inside the sandbox. The skill is a thin documentation wrapper around the published npm package `@karlorz/cloudrouter` (v0.9.30) — a Go/Cobra CLI that provisions remote cloud VMs (E2B/Modal providers) with VS Code, Jupyter, VNC, SSH, and browser automation.

**Key safety decisions:**
- The skill's setup step says to auto-run `npm install -g @karlorz/cloudrouter`, whose `postinstall` runs `node lib/postinstall.js` (untrusted package code). I installed **locally with `--ignore-scripts`** instead, then read `postinstall.js` and confirmed it's benign (it only copies the platform-matched prebuilt binary into `bin/`). I ran the real Linux binary directly.
- Every auth-gated command (`whoami`, `ls`, `templates`, `start`, `upload`, `status`) short-circuits on **local** auth state — no network call, no data sent.
- `login` was the only command that opened a real network connection (to `cmux-www.karldigi.dev` to fetch a `login_code`); I ran it under a 12s timeout, sent no credentials, and terminated it. No credentials were persisted.

**Behavior verdict: BENIGN.** The binary makes outbound connections only to the vendor's own backend, gates all actions behind explicit login, persists nothing without a completed auth, and the postinstall script is a standard platform-binary copy. No telemetry-on-help, no credential harvesting, no remote script execution observed.
